clue.text: Dr WMD's quarters for Karen

parts.note: Dr Hans Blix led the UN inspectors hunting weapons of mass destruction in Iraq
east and north are two quarters of the compass, abbreviated E and N

explanation.surface: A coded remark about a weapons inspector's lodgings being given over to a woman called Karen.
explanation.walkthrough: Karen is not just any woman: Karen Blixen was the Danish author of Out of Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Karen Blixen is the Danish writer, so her first name alone points to her surname here.

clue.text: Robber gang seized equipment

indicators.note: seized means one piece holds the other inside it

parts.note: a band is a group or gang
rig is equipment or gear

explanation.surface: A robber's gang grabbed some kit.
explanation.definitionFit: A brigand is a bandit, especially one of a gang preying on travellers.

clue.text: Old folk in Spain invading picnic with no clothes on

indicators.note: invading means one piece enters the other
stripped of its outer layer, so the word picnic loses its outside letters

parts.note: E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Elderly people in Spain gate-crash a nudist picnic.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iceni were the ancient British tribe led by Boudicca.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iceni were an ancient British tribe, a people of long ago.

clue.text: Beg child to abandon jump in Covent Garden

indicators.note: to abandon means to leave out, so the child is removed from the jump

parts.note: an entrechat is a ballet leap, as seen at the Royal Opera House, Covent Garden in London

explanation.surface: A plea for a youngster to stop leaping about in a London market square.
explanation.walkthrough: Covent Garden is home to the Royal Ballet, which suggests a ballet jump rather than any leap.
explanation.definitionFit: To entreat is to ask earnestly, the same as begging.

clue.text: Do I hear Paddy's mate drinks cocktails?

indicators.note: a question about hearing tells the solver to say the phrase and listen to its sound

parts.note: Paddy and Mick are both stock names for an Irishman, and to sup is to drink, giving MICK SUPS

explanation.surface: A listener wonders whether an Irishman's friend is sipping cocktails.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail is a mixture of ingredients, and mix-ups are jumbles or mixtures in the same loose sense.

clue.text: Rick Stein opening in Padstow's synchronised

indicators.note: to rick is to wrench or twist, so the next word is twisted into a new order
the opening of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Rick Stein, the TV chef, opens a restaurant in Padstow, a Cornish fishing port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rick' looks like the chef's first name, Rick Stein being a TV cook with restaurants in Padstow, but it is a verb meaning wrench, the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To be in step is to move in time with others, which is to be synchronised.

clue.text: Ulster loyalist maintains Latin library catalogue

indicators.note: maintains suggests holding something within, so one piece contains another

parts.note: a Unionist in Northern Ireland supports the union with Britain

explanation.surface: A Northern Irish loyalist keeps a list of Latin books.
explanation.definitionFit: A union list is a combined catalogue of the holdings of several libraries.

clue.text: A few steps required to keep emergency room bug-free

indicators.note: to keep is to hold inside, so one piece goes within another

parts.note: a stile is a set of steps over a fence or wall

explanation.surface: An emergency room must be kept spotless after a few steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Sterile means free from germs, so a bug-free place is sterile.

clue.text: With 99 getting in, Left versus Right produced result in 1997

indicators.note: getting in places the number inside the longer phrase

parts.note: Labour is the left-wing UK party
the Tories are the right-wing UK party
ninety-nine in Roman numerals can be written IC

explanation.surface: A contest of left and right in the 1997 election with 99 seats changing hands.
explanation.walkthrough: In 1997 the Labour Party won the UK general election by a landslide. IC for 99 is an informal Roman form.
explanation.definitionFit: The British general election of 1997 ended in a landslide win for Tony Blair's party.

clue.text: Today's emergency number

definitions.meaning: the puzzle appeared on 9 September 2009, a date written 9/9/09
the UK telephone number for police, fire and ambulance

explanation.walkthrough: The British emergency number is triple nine, the equivalent of 911 in the US; the date of publication supplies the other sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The date 9/9/9 and the UK telephone code for emergency services both read as three nines in a row.

clue.text: Good news for rail commuters except one, dumbstruck

indicators.note: one is the Roman numeral I, and except asks for it to be left out

parts.note: when the train's fixed, commuters can travel again

explanation.surface: Rail commuters are delighted by good news, apart from one who is left speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'except one' drops an I from TRAIN'S FIXED.
explanation.definitionFit: To be transfixed is to be rooted to the spot in amazement, the same as being struck dumb.

clue.text: It's nearly May 19 and opening of exotic Rio dance

indicators.note: nearly means the word May loses its final letter

parts.note: nineteen in Roman numerals is XIX

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter, here taken from exotic

explanation.surface: Late spring brings the start of an exotic dance in Rio.
explanation.definitionFit: The maxixe is a Brazilian dance from Rio de Janeiro, a forerunner of the tango.

clue.text: Small change in 27 and 9, not far short of 17%

indicators.note: a small change to the letters of an entry is a mild rearrangement of them

parts.note: the answer to 27 across, the old way of writing today's date in nines
nine in Roman numerals is IX

explanation.surface: Loose coins added to a pair of numbers come to a little less than a sixth.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'small change' is only a slight shuffle of the 27-across entry, and the 9 is read as a Roman numeral rather than the triple-nine entry.
explanation.definitionFit: One in six is 16.67 per cent, a fraction just below seventeen per cent.

clue.text: Say nice things about new tux, creating bit of a stir?

indicators.note: about places one word around another, here admiring words enclosing the rest

parts.note: to admire someone is to speak or think well of them

indicators.note: something new is remade, so these letters take a fresh order

explanation.surface: Compliments about a new tuxedo cause a small sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' is the anagram signal for the dinner jacket; 'stir' suggests a commotion but here means mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: An admixture is something stirred into a mixture, a small added ingredient.

clue.text: Sixth sense needed in teaching

parts.note: tuition is instruction or teaching

explanation.surface: Instinct is said to be what a good teacher requires.
explanation.definitionFit: Intuition is knowledge without reasoning, often called a sixth sense beyond the usual five.

clue.text: See 9
Their lives appear many times here in musical

definitions.text: Their lives appear many times here in musical

parts.words: Their lives appear many times here in musical
parts.note: creatures said to have nine lives, and the nines appear many times in this grid; they also give their name to a Lloyd Webber musical

explanation.walkthrough: The animals are traditionally said to have nine lives, tying them to this puzzle full of nines.
explanation.definitionFit: Felines are proverbially granted nine lives, and they also title a famous stage musical.

clue.text: Hillary keen about visiting Sri Lanka and Norway as …

indicators.note: visiting puts one piece inside the other places named

parts.note: CL is the international vehicle code for Sri Lanka (formerly Ceylon)
N is the international vehicle code for Norway
to be into something is to be keen on it

explanation.surface: Hillary is so taken with a trip to Sri Lanka and Norway that she sets off a chain of clues.
explanation.definitionFit: Hillary Clinton is the American politician, so her first name points to her surname.

clue.text: Tom the cowboy departs in a huff without starting some plumbing

parts.note: Tom Mix was a star of silent Western films

indicators.note: being in a huff suggests an upset, so the remaining letters are thrown into disorder
without its starting letter, the word departs loses its first character

explanation.surface: A Western film star storms off in a temper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without starting' removes D from DEPARTS; 'in a huff' turns EPARTS into ERTAPS.
explanation.definitionFit: Mixer taps blend hot and cold water through one spout, a kind of plumbing fitting.

clue.text: … a former Republican opponent's persuaded to clarify why …

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: persuaded suggests being talked round, so the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: Sarah Palin was the Republican vice-presidential candidate in 2008, opposing the Democrats

explanation.surface: A one-time Republican rival has been talked into explaining her reasons.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipses link the three clues: Sarah Palin was the 2008 Republican vice-presidential candidate, so she is a rival to Hillary's party.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain something is to make it clear, which is what clarify means.

clue.text: … she's going nuts finally behind her picket fences

indicators.note: behind puts these letters after the woman just named

parts.note: the woman of the previous clue, Sarah Palin

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: A woman is driven crazy at last behind her picket fence.
explanation.walkthrough: The three clues run together, so 'her' carries Palin on from 18 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Palings are pointed wooden stakes, the uprights that make up a picket fence.

clue.text: Month when Israelis at last have riotous time

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word before
riotous suggests disorder, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A month in which Israelis finally have a wild time.
explanation.definitionFit: Shevat is the fifth month of the Jewish civil year, falling in January and February.

clue.text: Early "Top Gear" programme begins with Exhibit A crash, driving off Beachy Head

indicators.note: begins takes the first letter of programme
a crash smashes things up, so the letters are thrown about
driving off removes a letter from the phrase
a head is the top or first letter of the word Beachy

explanation.surface: A motoring show opens with a smash at Beachy Head, a famous chalk cliff on the south coast of England.
explanation.walkthrough: Top Gear is a BBC motoring show, but the definition reads it literally as headwear; 'driving off' takes away the head of Beachy before 'crash' scrambles what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: A pixie hat is a pointed knitted cap worn by babies, so it is headgear from early life.

clue.text: Opts for Ernie, say the photoshopped bits?

indicators.note: say asks for the phrase to be spoken and heard

parts.note: to opt for is to pick, and Ernie Els is a South African golfer, giving PICKS ELS

explanation.surface: Someone chooses a golfer, perhaps in an edited photograph.
explanation.definitionFit: Pixels are the tiny dots that make up a digital image, which photo editing alters.

clue.text: Gas turned up to No IX

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: read as No I X: no one is NONE, followed by the X

explanation.surface: A gas is pushed up to a ninth position.
explanation.walkthrough: IX splits so that 'No I' reads as 'no one', giving NONE, leaving X; the run NONEX is then turned up.
explanation.definitionFit: Xenon is a noble gas, element 54, used in lamps and headlights.

clue.text: US night bird, second aviatrix to fly over river

indicators.note: over here means placed around, so the rearranged letters cover the river
flying suggests the letters are scattered and recombined

explanation.surface: A pilot takes a second to fly over a river at night.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to fly' makes TRIXVAIA from AVIATRIX, with R inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Strix varia is the scientific name of the barred owl, a North American bird of the night.

clue.text: See 9
Number making ice creams with 9, 15 and 25

definitions.text: Number making ice creams with 9, 15 and 25

parts.words: Number making ice creams with 9, 15 and 25
parts.note: a number which, put beside nine, names the British soft ice-cream cone with a flake in it

explanation.walkthrough: A 99 is a British ice-cream cone with a chocolate flake; the linked 9, 15, 25 supply the nine.
explanation.definitionFit: Ninety is a number, and ninety-nine names a well-known ice-cream cone in Britain.

clue.text: Today's old 9, 15 and 25 collectively

parts.note: the three linked entries each give nine, so together they are nines

explanation.surface: The date today, in old style, is the triple entry gathered together.
explanation.walkthrough: The puzzle appeared on 09.09.09, a date made of three 'o-nines'.
explanation.definitionFit: The publication date 09/09/09 is written as three zero-nines, so it is all o-nines.
